texts.value: NADPH-dependent reductase that can degrade the nitrate ester explosives pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN) and nitroglycerin (also known as glycerol trinitrate, GTN), thereby enabling them to serve as nitrogen sources for growth (PubMed:8919782, PubMed:8932320). It catalyzes the NADPH-dependent denitration of PETN, releasing nitrite and producing pentaerythritol trinitrate and pentaerythritol dinitrate (PubMed:8919782). The reaction follows a ping-pong mechanism (PubMed:8932320). It can also use nitroglycerin as a substrate (PubMed:8919782, PubMed:8932320). It can reduce 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT), yielding hydride- and dihydride-Meisenheimer complexes and nitrite, suggesting that E.cloacae PB2 can use TNT as the sole nitrogen source (PubMed:15184158, PubMed:9687442). It can use ethylene glycol dinitrate (EGDN), with low efficiency (PubMed:8919782, PubMed:8932320). In addition, the enzyme can bind and use steroid ligands (PubMed:11428899). Some steroids act as substrates while others are inhibitors (PubMed:11428899). The enzyme can reduce prednisone and 1,4-androstadiene-3,17-dione, but not progesterone or 4-androstene-3,17-dione (PubMed:11428899). It can reduce the unsaturated bond of the alpha/beta-unsaturated ketone cyclohex-2-enone, which is used widely as a generic substrate of the OYE family, but it cannot use codeinone, the best known substrate for morphinone reductase (PubMed:15184158, PubMed:8932320). It can use trans-2-hexenal and two compounds related to TNT, 1-nitrocyclohexene and 2-nitrobenzaldehyde (PubMed:15184158). In vitro, it shows highest activity against nitrate esters, and lower activity towards TNT and alpha/beta-unsaturated carbonyls (PubMed:15184158)
